clue.text: Harbour needs bush for nursery merry-go-round

definitions.meaning: the ... harbours were the floating prefabricated ports towed across the Channel for D-Day
children circle this bush in the nursery rhyme 'Here we go round the ... bush'

explanation.surface: A port is somehow fitted out with shrubbery for a children's playground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the name: the wartime portable port and the fruit tree in the circling nursery song.

clue.text: Its first runner was late arriving in Athens

definitions.text: Its first runner was late arriving in Athens

parts.words: Its first runner was late arriving in Athens
parts.note: the legendary messenger Pheidippides ran to Athens with news of victory and died on arrival, so 'late' means dead as well as tardy

explanation.surface: The first competitor in some race reached Athens behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead: Pheidippides delivered the news of the Greek victory and collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-distance race commemorates the messenger's run from the battlefield to Athens.

clue.text: County variety of mail horse

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A local breed of horse once used for carrying post.
explanation.walkthrough: Loamshire is the fictional English county used by novelists to stand for any rural shire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an invented English shire that writers use as a typical rural setting.

clue.text: Race spirit discernible in a Dorset hostelry

indicators.note: discernible in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patriotic feeling can be sensed in a West Country pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit of a people or community is its guiding character.

clue.text: Line of travel included in the drill

indicators.note: included says the word in is put into the route

parts.note: a route is the line of a journey

explanation.surface: The path you take is part of the regular exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill is the usual procedure, the set sequence one always follows.

clue.text: High flier ditched through over-heating

parts.note: the Greek myth of the boy whose wax-and-feather wings melted when he flew too near the sun, so he fell into the sea

explanation.surface: An aviator had to land in the sea when the engine overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Daedalus's son flew too close to the sun, the wax in his wings melted and he plunged into the sea.

clue.text: When Henry V speaks " the air, a — libertine, is still'

definitions.text: When Henry V speaks " the air, a — libertine, is still'

parts.words: When Henry V speaks " the air, a — libertine, is still'
parts.note: a quotation from the Archbishop in Henry V, Act 1: the missing word means licensed, free to roam

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line describes how even the free-roaming air falls silent to hear the king speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The word fills the gap in Shakespeare's line, meaning granted a charter and so free to roam.

clue.text: Sharp girl begins to make an instrument

indicators.note: begins says only the opening part of the girl's name is wanted

parts.note: Becky Sharp of Thackeray's Vanity Fair is Rebecca

explanation.surface: A clever young woman starts to build a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like a musical term but is the surname of Thackeray's heroine; only the start of her first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: Look pleased about one literary comparison

indicators.note: about says the smile goes round the numeral

parts.note: to smile is to look pleased
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A writer looks happy at a comparison in someone's prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech likening one thing to another with 'like' or 'as' is the classic literary comparison.

clue.text: Ornament to be put on top of a ship

indicators.note: in a down clue put on means placed above, so the first word comes before the second

parts.note: taken as written
the deck is the top surface of a ship

explanation.surface: Something decorative is to be mounted on a ship's upper level.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to adorn or deck it out with decoration.

clue.text: By the way Christ Church caters for travellers

definitions.note: read as '(a place that) caters for travellers', a noun sense

parts.note: the way is the road, so something by the way stands on the road
the Oxford college Christ Church is traditionally known as 'the House'

explanation.surface: Incidentally, an Oxford college provides hospitality to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' poses as 'incidentally'. Christ Church, Oxford, is nicknamed 'the House' by its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside inn is a place that serves food and drink to people on a journey.

clue.text: It holds family records (revolutionary or not)

definitions.text: It holds family records (revolutionary or not)

parts.words: It holds family records (revolutionary or not)
parts.note: a book of family photographs keeps family records; a set of gramophone discs is records that revolve on a turntable, the photo kind does not

explanation.surface: A book keeps a family's history, whether the family were rebels or conformists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics but means spinning on a turntable: the word covers both a photo book and a set of discs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound book for photographs or stamps, and also a collection of recorded music, both bear this name.

clue.text: Ivory from Monmouthshire river town in a back-street

indicators.note: the town sits in the turned street, so the street's letters enclose it
back says the street abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Usk is a town on the river of the same name in Monmouthshire, Wales

explanation.surface: Ivory is found in an alley in a Welsh market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' reads as one word for an alley; split it so 'back' turns the street abbreviation round. Usk is a small town on the river of that name in south-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusks are the main source of ivory, so the material stands for them.

clue.text: I study it backwards, state it's the same

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

indicators.note: backwards says the word it is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone working on a text in reverse declares that it reads the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I study it backwards' reads as a palindrome hunt, but only 'it' is turned, giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike are one and the same.

clue.text: Love cereal, if put inside the mouth

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: put inside says the little word if goes into the cereal

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Feed yourself rice with affection: put it in your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Any opening of a body or vessel is an orifice, and the mouth is the most familiar.

clue.text: Fly from one Munich imbroglio

indicators.note: an imbroglio is a confused tangle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a single tangled affair in Munich.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon fly is a parasitic wasp-like insect that lays eggs in other larvae.

clue.text: Dam where Kipling's snake swallowed a bone

indicators.note: the snake swallows the bone, so its letters wrap round it

parts.note: Kaa is the python in Kipling's Jungle Book
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: Somewhere a snake from the Jungle Book gulped down a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: A snake swallowing a bone is apt for a python. The Kariba Dam is on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kariba is the great hydroelectric barrier across the Zambezi on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

clue.text: Stick on soles making it hard to walk?

definitions.text: Stick on soles making it hard to walk?

parts.words: Stick on soles making it hard to walk?
parts.note: not adhesive soles for shoes but a stick beaten on the soles of the feet, a punishment that leaves the victim unable to walk

explanation.surface: Glued-on shoe soles that make walking difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick on' looks like gluing; read 'stick' as a cane applied to the soles of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a torture of caning the soles of the feet, leaving the victim hobbled.

clue.text: Sicily's mountain-climb takes in one place for a liqueur

indicators.note: takes in says the turned mountain wraps round the other letters
in a down clue climb says the word goes upward, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily
the Roman numeral I is one
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Climbing Etna includes a stop somewhere for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' turns ETNA into ANTE, which takes in I and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: A way of acting

parts.note: read as an ordinary way of doing things, and as Stanislavski's acting system where actors live the part

explanation.surface: This is a style of behaviour or performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is a way of doing something, and the Stanislavski system is a famous school of stage performance.

clue.text: Tell someone the way that is straight.

definitions.meaning: to show a person how to get somewhere is to give directions
a straight route or answer is one without detours

explanation.surface: Give someone frank directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide a person is to point them on their way, and a non-stop route is unswerving.

clue.text: A learned cleric has one boy, Joseph

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by a learned cleric
the Roman numeral I is one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An erudite clergyman has a single son called Joseph.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison (1672-1719) was the English essayist who co-founded The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph is the first name of the English essayist of The Spectator.

clue.text: Slander Parsees perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Defamation of Zoroastrians, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander is to cast damaging aspersions on someone.

clue.text: A crazy one ? Point to Gaul's romantic hero

parts.note: mad means crazy
the Roman numeral I is one
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A crazy person points to a French hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Amadis of Gaul is the hero of the Spanish and Portuguese chivalric romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadis de Gaula is the knight of the famous chivalric romance.

clue.text: Play catching a conscience — or vermin ?

definitions.text: Play catching a conscience — or vermin ?

parts.words: Play catching a conscience — or vermin ?
parts.note: Hamlet's play-within-a-play, staged to 'catch the conscience of the king', has a name that also means a trap for small rodents

explanation.surface: Is this drama meant to snare a guilty mind, or pests?
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet the prince renames his play to trap Claudius's guilt; Agatha Christie's long-running play took the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls the play he stages to expose Claudius by the name of a device that catches rodents.

clue.text: Total put in circulation

definitions.meaning: total in the sense of complete or absolute
to pass counterfeit money or to issue it is the legal sense

explanation.surface: The whole sum was issued as currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete describes a thorough failure, and passing forged coins was the old offence of issuing them.

clue.text: Booked as master carpenter

definitions.meaning: the schoolmaster in James Hilton's book 'Goodbye, Mr ...' is known by this name
a ship's carpenter is traditionally nicknamed this, after the wood shavings

explanation.surface: Reserved as the head craftsman of a woodwork shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means 'in a book', not reserved: the gentle teacher of Hilton's novel 'Goodbye, Mr Chips'.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's schoolmaster bears the nickname, and sailors have long given the same nickname to the ship's woodworker.

clue.text: It's near the cathedral

parts.note: an adjective for near, and the ... grounds round a cathedral share the same spelling

explanation.surface: Something is located beside the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's precinct is the enclosed area surrounding it, and the same word means nearby.

clue.text: The line we're given ?

parts.note: a surveyor's reference level is the line of this name, and the Latin word means 'thing given'

explanation.surface: Is this the official story we have been handed?
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'given', it is a fact taken as a starting point, and a reference line in surveying.

clue.text: Troops can be destroyed by St Elmo's fire

indicators.note: be destroyed says the letters of the fodder are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Soldiers might be wiped out by a mysterious glowing fire.
explanation.definitionFit: St Elmo's fire, the electrical glow on ships' masts, is also called by this name from Italian 'holy body'.

clue.text: Something lyrical about a redhead's garment

indicators.note: the song goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a song is something with lyrics
the head of red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A lyric is written in praise of a ginger-haired woman's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Writer appears to run away with her

definitions.note: the woman in question, a female name

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: An author seems to be running off with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'her', a woman's name; the irony is that Odysseus's wife was the model of fidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name, most famously Odysseus's faithful wife.
